column2: You two, widely praised and strengthened by homage, rule by the greatness of skill, O pure in vow, by the longest ways.
Praised by Jamadagni, sit in the seat of truth; drink the soma, O strengtheners of truth.
May your two long-maned bay horses, prayer-yoked, carry you, Indra; hear our prayers.
We, the Brahmins, soma-offerers, with the yoked bay horses, call you, the soma-drinker Indra, having pressed.
Come, Indra and Agni, to the pressed soma, the desired one praised with songs; drink of it, urged by our thought.
Indra and Agni, together with the singer, the conscious sacrifice goes forth; drink this pressed soma.
I choose Indra and Agni, with the covering of the wise, for the drive of the sacrifice; let them be satisfied here with the soma.
Milking the divine honey from the udder, the dear, he sat in the ancient seat; you flow, a racer to be asked, upholding, washed by men, the all-seeing.
The well-armed god, the drop, flows, slayer of slander, guarding the ways; father of the gods, begetter, most skilful, the prop of heaven, support of the earth.
The sage, the inspired leader of the peoples, Ribhu, steadfast, with the poetry of Ushanas; he indeed knew the hidden, secret name of the cows.
None like you, divine or earthly, has been born or will be born; desiring horses, bounteous Indra, with strength, desiring cattle, we call you.
What true, most exhilarating drink of the stalk delights you? You break even the firm to win wealth.
Be to us a helper of friends and singers, a hundredfold, for protection.
We ask for the heaven-dwelling, good giver, surrounded by powers, like a mountain, much-nourishing, wealth with cattle, hundreds and thousands, swiftly.
Him whom neither the violent nor the obstinate turn aside in the joys of the drink, who with reverence gives a worthy praise to the singer who presses.
The demon-slayer, all-seeing, goes to his iron-free nest; he sat in the seat in the trough.
Be the best giver of room, the greatest, the best Vritra-slayer; you carry the bounty of the bounteous.
He who, having drunk of you, the bull acts as a bull; having drunk of it, the heaven-finder, the well-marked, has come forward for food, like Etasha for the strength.
This victor-gainer flows, pressed for Indra's carrying; the soma is known for the victory as he wishes.
In the joys of this, Indra takes hold of the victor's grasp, and bears the thunderbolt, the bull, conqueror in the waters.
The pressed one flows around with the purifying stream, the drop, like a skilled horse.
Men, press that hard-to-seize soma with all-turning thought; let the stones be for the sacrifice.
The tongue of truth flows, the dear honey, the speaker, lord of this thought, unconquerable; the son holds the secret name of the parents, the third light of heaven.
Shining, he has roared down into the vessels, held by men in the golden receptacle; they praised the milkings of truth; on the three-backed one you shine over the dawns.
Grandson of strength, desiring us, may we give to him who gives offerings; may he be a helper in battles, a strengthener, and protector of bodies.
Wherever your mind sets its skill higher, there you make your seat.
For your fullness has not disappeared, O lord of the ends; therefore you win worship.
We approach you in the work for help; may that youth, the fierce, who dares, come; we choose you, the kindled helper, friends, Indra, the victor.
They strengthen you, hero, with prayers in the barley-fields, you who have grown, O stone-bearer, day by day.
They yoke the two bay horses to the song of the swift one, on the wide chariot with a wide yoke, speech-yoked, carriers of Indra, finders of heaven.
Sing to Indra, the best protector of your drink, the all-conquering, hundred-powered, greatest of the peoples.
Invoked by many, praised by many, heard in ancient songs — call him Indra.
Indra is our giver of great strengths, the dancer; may the great one restrain.
Let the good givers praise the hymn and the heavenly one, as men; we have made for the true-bountiful.
You, Indra, desiring strength; you, hundred-powered, desiring cattle; you, O Vasu, desiring gold.
Never indeed have I drunk of another, thunderbolt-bearer, in the newest of works; by your hymns alone is it known.
The gods seek the one who presses; they do not long for sleep; the untiring go to carelessness.
Let our songs resound around for exhilarating Indra pressed; let the singers sing the hymn.
In whom all glories rejoice, the seven assemblies — we call Indra at the pressing.
The gods stretched out the conscious sacrifice in the Trikadrukas; let our songs strengthen him.
O strong one, for worship of the strong, for the delight, your soma is pressed; O Akhandala, you are invoked.
Your horn-bull, grandson, great-grandson, the cup-drinker — set the mind upon him.
Now, Indra, grasp for us the wondrous, abundant grasp, great-handed, with your right hand.
We know you, much active, much giving, much bounteous, of great measure, with your helps.
Neither gods nor mortals restrain you, O hero, when you wish to give, as they do not hold back a terrible cow.
Let not the foolish, nor the mockers, nor the harmful hurt you; do not love the hater of prayer.
May they gladden you here, the cow-surrounded, for great wealth; drink like a wild buffalo at a lake.
Drink, O Vasu, this pressed drink, filling the belly; fearless, may we be yours.
Washed by men, pressed by stones, purified through woolen sieves, like a horse cleansed in rivers.
We have made your barley sweet with cows, delighting it, Indra, in this shared feast.
Whoever is in your own way, at the pressing, steady your body; let that soma-drink delight you.
May it reach your belly, Indra; may the prayer reach your head; may your arms, O hero, with wealth.
Come and sit; sing to Indra, friends, bearing the hymn.
Indra, the greatest of many, ruler of desirable things, in the pressed soma together.
May he be at our yoking, for wealth, for abundance; may he come to us with strengths.
I call after the ancient dwelling the man of many fronts, whom your father called before.
May he come, if he hears, with thousandfold helps and strengths to our call.
He grows in the first heaven, in the seat of the gods; good to cross, most famous, a conqueror in the waters.
I call on Indra, strong, for the winning of strength, for the battle; be our nearest in favor, a friend for growth.
With this homage I call Agni, the grandson of strength; dear, most conscious, unhurried, of good sacrifice, the immortal messenger of all.
He yokes the ruddy two that feed all, he runs well-offered; the good prayer, sacrifice, good pacifier of the Vasus, the god's bounty to the people.
The daughter of heaven, coming, has been seen, shining; the great one uncovers the waters; with her eye she makes darkness into light, O fair one.
The Sun together releases the cows, rising like a flaming star; at your dawning and the sun's, may we be united with our share.
You, O men, gave wondrous food; urge on the truthful one; bring your chariot together, of one mind, and drink the soma honey.
After his ancient light the unfailing milked the bright one, the milk, the sage of a thousand songs.
This one is like the sun in sight; this one runs to the lakes, the seven streams to heaven.
This stands above all worlds, purifying, Soma the god, like the sun.
This god, by ancient birth, is pressed for the gods; the bay one flows in the filter.
This god, by ancient thought, around the gods; the seer grows by the sage.
Milking the ancient milk, you are poured into the filter; roaring, you begat the gods.
Bring near to the one who stands, and set fear on the enemy; flowing, find wealth.
The gods have gone to the drop just born, water-crossing, adorned with the milk of cows.
The brown, bright ones have flowed to the vessels with the stream of truth, bringing strength rich in cattle.
Pressed for Indra, Vayu, Varuna, the Maruts, may the somas flow to Vishnu.
The beloved bright one is covered in the garment, dear like a son to be cleansed; the workers send him as a chariot into the rivers from the hands.
The exhilaration-dropping somas have gone forth for our fame and that of the bounteous, pressed at the ritual.
Then like a swan to its flock he longed for the thought of all; like a horse he is anointed with cows.
Then the women of Trita cleanse the bay one with stones, the drop for Indra to drink.
Flow with this, god-seeking, roaring; you pass through the filter on all sides; the streams of honey have been released.
Flow, Soma, first of speech, with wondrous helps, to all poetry.
You, first, rousing the oceanic waters and speech — flow, all-seeing one.
For you, wise one, these worlds stand in greatness, Soma; for you the cows run.
In your friendship, O drop, may we overcome those who attack, in your highest splendor.
Your terrible, sharp weapons which exist for the destroyer — protect us from every reviler.
Of you, the bull, is the bull's vigor; the bull is the forest, the bull is pressed; you, bull, are indeed the bull.
Like a neighing horse, a bull, drop, join cattle and horses; open for us the doors to wealth.
When you are sprinkled with the waters, cleansed by the Ayus, you reach the shared seat in the trough.
Flow to us heroic strength, joyful, well-armed; come here indeed, O drop.
We choose friendship of you who flow, as we make the filter flow.
With those waves of yours that flow with a stream onto the filter, be gracious to us, Soma.
Purified, bring us wealth and heroic food, ruling on all sides, O Soma.
They always call Agni, lord of the people, with offerings — bearer of oblations, dear to many.
O Agni, bring the gods here, born for him who spreads the grass; you are our priest, worthy of praise.
We call Mitra and Varuna to drink the soma, who are born of pure skill.
By truth, you two who strengthen truth, lords of the light of truth — I call Mitra and Varuna.
May Varuna be helper, and Mitra with all helps; make us rich in bounty.
Indra caused the sun to rise in heaven for long sight; he sent the mountain apart with the cows.
We offer a great homage, well-praised, to Indra and Agni; with thought we seek help for our cows.
For them forever the sages invoke thus for help, together, for the winning of strength.
We, praisers, with songs, offering food, call you two, bringers of wisdom, desiring to win.
